CVE-2026-111751.title: Angular: Denial of Service via RouterLink Query Parameter Retention in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
CVE-2026-111751.description: Angular is a development platform for building mobile and desktop web applications using TypeScript/JavaScript and other languages. From 21.2.0 until 21.2.25 and 22.2.1, RouterLink directives rendered during Node.js server-side rendering retain computed UrlTree instances for the lifetime of each request. When queryParamsHandling is set to merge or preserve, either per link or through defaultQueryParamsHandling, every rendered link can retain a copy of attacker-controlled query parameters in its UrlTree. When upstream proxies or load balancers forward oversized query strings without rejecting them at the edge, multiple affected links and overlapping renders can amplify heap use until the Node.js old-space heap is exhausted and the SSR worker terminates. Numeric query-parameter names increase allocation pressure but are not required, memory is released after rendering completes, and pure client-side SPAs are not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 21.2.25 and 22.2.1.

CVE-2026-116251.title: pgAdmin 4: A user's other sessions survive a change of their password
CVE-2026-116251.description:
pgAdmin 4 did not invalidate a user's existing sessions when their password changed, either through the user's own change password dialog or through an administrator resetting it in User Management. A session established before the change, for example on another device or by someone who had obtained the old password or a session cookie, therefore stayed logged in after the change, which is the step a user or administrator takes precisely to cut such access off. It remained usable until it expired.

The fix rotates the user's session identifier (fs_uniquifier) whenever the password is changed, so every other session of that user is logged out. The session that made the change is logged in again and keeps its database connections. Saved server passwords, including those for shared servers, are re-encrypted under the new key; any that cannot be decrypted are cleared and the user is told. If re-encryption fails, the sessions are still revoked and the saved passwords are cleared rather…

CVE-2026-99707.title: mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio
CVE-2026-99707.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH. Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released. Another collapse can replace and free it. With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs. A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio. This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held. The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

CVE-2026-99790.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set

nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() once for each
requested listener and passes flags of 0, so every listener registers with
rpcbind on its own. A rpcbind that accepts the connection and never replies
therefore costs one timeout for each entry. With the cap of 1024 entries
the request can hold nfsd_mutex for about 34 minutes, which is roughly 17
times the hung-task threshold.

One failure is enough to know that the next call will not fare better.
Read svc_rpcb_failure_count() before the create loop, and pass
SVC_SOCK_ANONYMOUS for the rest of the request once the count moves.
